s1.syndrome_frame: A slowly growing eyelid mass with recent changes and crust formation
salient_findings: Yellowish-brown, well-circumscribed papule on the central lower eyelid
Flakier surface at one lateral end
Hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts and neoplastic squamous cell proliferation
key_facts: 4-year history of a left lower eyelid mass
Recent growth and crust formation
Mass is a yellowish-brown, well-circumscribed papule
Papule is located on the central lower eyelid
No margin involvement
Flakier surface at one lateral end
Specimen measured 0.8 × 0.5 × 0.3 cm
Hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts
Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells
Malignant squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli
Mitotic figures are present
Ki67 staining highlights scattered basal cells and 20-40% of tumor cell nuclei

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli, mitotic figures, and Ki67 staining patterns are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Keratoacanthoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts and a flakier surface at one lateral end are characteristic features of this condition

shortlist.label: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells into the dermis and involvement of many hairs support this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Bowen disease
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic lesion and malignant squamous cells are consistent with this diagnosis, although the presence of invasive features makes it less likely

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma in situ
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant squamous cells and hyperkeratotic lesion are consistent with this diagnosis, although the presence of invasive features makes it less likely

raw.rationale: The presence of malignant squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli, along with mitotic figures and the proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells pushing down into the dermis, supports the diagnosis of invasive squamous cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Too broad, as it does not specify the invasive nature of the tumor

rejected.label: Keratoacanthoma
rejected.why: Typically has a more rapid growth phase and a central crater-like appearance, which is not described in the case

rejected.label: Bowen disease
rejected.why: Is a form of squamous cell carcinoma in situ, which does not invade the dermis, contradicting the microscopic findings

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma in situ
rejected.why: Does not invade the dermis, which contradicts the microscopic findings of neoplastic cells pushing down into the dermis
